Focus Fence blocks distracting sites for your whole phone using a local VPN that filters only DNS — the phone\'s address lookups. All filtering decisions happen on your phone: no account, no server. Lookups that aren\'t blocked go to a public DNS resolver (Cloudflare or Google), as they normally would. It\'s designed to use very little battery, and Settings → Logs & diagnostics measures how much it actually uses.

Flip the switch on the main screen and accept Android\'s VPN prompt to start blocking.

Tip: for blocking that survives reboots, enable Always-on VPN for Focus Fence in Android\'s network settings.
Four ways to block a site

On the Blocklist tab, tap + to add a domain like reddit.com, and pick how it\'s blocked:

• Block always — the default.

• Block during set hours — for example 9:00–18:00 every day. Windows can wrap midnight, like 22:00–06:00.

• Daily time limit — for example 10 minutes per day, then it\'s blocked until midnight.

• Allow only specific sections — block a site except the parts you choose (next page).

Tap any domain in the list to change its rule later. Blocking a domain always covers its subdomains too: reddit.com also blocks old.reddit.com.
Allow only parts of a site

Want Facebook Marketplace without the feed? That\'s a section rule:

1. On the Blocklist tab, tap + and enter facebook.com (or tap an existing domain).

2. Choose Allow only specific sections.

3. Type /marketplace — the "section" is whatever comes after the domain in the address, so facebook.com/marketplace → /marketplace. Add several separated by commas, like /marketplace, /events.

4. When prompted, enable the Focus Fence accessibility service. Section rules work by reading your browser\'s address bar, and Android requires that permission for it. The address bar is compared against your own rules and is not sent anywhere. It is saved on this phone only if you turn on Record browser addresses in Logs & diagnostics.

From then on, any facebook.com page that isn\'t under /marketplace is backed out of automatically, with a small "Blocked by Focus Fence" notice.

Browsers only: the Facebook app has no address bar to read, so open marketplace in your browser (Chrome, Firefox, Brave, Edge, Samsung Internet and others all work).

Honesty section — the limits of DNS-based blocking:

• Pages your phone looked up recently may still load for a few minutes after you block them (DNS caching).

• Time limits are estimates based on lookup activity — accurate to within a minute or two, and only screen-on time counts.

• Time limits count and enforce only a site\'s main web addresses (facebook.com, www., m. …) — hidden app/SDK traffic like graph.facebook.com neither drains a budget nor breaks when it runs out. Changing a limit resets that day\'s count.

• Apps in VPN exclusions bypass the filter entirely — use it for your own apps that talk to a limited site\'s servers.

• Turn off Private DNS in Android\'s network settings, or it will carry lookups around the filter. (The common browser tricks are already guarded against.)

• Android allows only one VPN at a time, so Focus Fence can\'t run alongside a regular VPN.

• Video ads on YouTube or Twitch can\'t be removed — they come from the same domains as the videos themselves.

• And you can always just switch it off. It\'s a fence, not a prison — Always-on VPN adds friction if you want more commitment.

Strict mode keeps future-you honest. While it\'s on, turning blocking off, removing rules, or un-blocking apps requires requesting an unlock, waiting 10 minutes, and making your change inside a 5-minute window. Adding new blocks is always allowed. (Pair it with Always-on VPN for the strongest fence.)

App blocking closes whole apps the moment they open — use it for the Facebook or TikTok apps, which DNS and section rules can\'t reach. Choose apps from the "App & section blocking" card; it uses the same accessibility permission as section rules.

Stats (the chart icon up top) shows what was blocked today, your time-budget usage, and a 7-day trend. Counts only ever live on your phone, and only the last 14 days are kept.

1. On the Blocklist tab, tap + and add your own domains — or use Add all social media presets there.

2. Tap any domain to set hours, a daily limit, or allowed sections; block whole apps from the same tab.

3. On Settings, optionally switch on Block ads & trackers — it downloads a 100k+ domain filter list once and blocks ads device-wide.

4. On Home, flip the switch and accept the VPN prompt.

You can reopen this guide anytime from the ? icon at the top.
